;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[2016–18 Kashmir unrest]]
**Clashes in [[Kashmir, India|South Kashmir]]{{Disambiguation needed|date=April 2020}}, [[India]], kill two civilians, three soldiers, and 13 militants. [https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/encounters-underway-in-shopian-13-terrorists-gunned-down/articleshow/63564305.cms? (''The Times of India'')]
*[[2018 Gaza border protests]]
**The [[Government of Israel|Israeli Government]] rejects calls for an inquiry, with [[Prime Minister of Israel|Prime Minister]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] likening criticism by [[Turkey|Turkish]] [[President of Turkey|President]] [[Recep Tayyip Erdogan]] to an [[April Fool's Day]] joke. [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2018/04/01/israel-rejects-calls-gaza-inquiry-netanyahu-likens-criticism/ (''The Telegraph'')]
**[[Pope Francis]] uses his [[Easter]] address [[Pope Francis#International diplomatic role|to call for peace]] between the peoples of Israel and [[State of Palestine|Palestine]] in response to the clashes. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2018/apr/01/pope-francis-easter-plea-for-peace-after-gaza-deaths (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Syrian Civil War]]
**Rebel fighters start evacuating from [[Douma, Syria|Douma]], Eastern [[Ghouta]], [[Syria]], and head to [[Idlib Governorate]] on government buses. Douma is the last rebel stronghold in Eastern Ghouta. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/middle_east/small-number-of-rebels-start-to-leave-syrias-douma/2018/04/01/bb4d4fc6-3594-11e8-af3c-2123715f78df_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
*[[Guatemalan Civil War]]
**The trial of [[Guatemala|Guatemalan]] ex-ruler [[Efraín Ríos Montt]], accused of [[genocide]] during the civil war in the 1980s, ends abruptly with the defendant's death. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-latin-america-43611867 (BBC)]
;Business and economy
*[[Bahrain]]i state media reports the discovery of the nation's largest known deposit of [[petroleum|oil and gas]] in an offshore field. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-04-01/bahrain-says-its-biggest-oil-find-since-1932-dwarfs-reserves (Bloomberg)]
*[[Iraq]]'s Oil Ministry brings forward the proposed date for awarding oil exploration contracts for new fields offshore and near the [[Iran]]ian and [[Kuwait]]i borders to April 15. [https://www.cnbc.com/2018/04/01/oil-iraq-bumps-up-the-date-for-awarding-new-contracts-to-april-15.html (CNBC)]
;Disasters and accidents
*[[2018 Kemerovo fire]]
**[[Governor (Russia)|Governor]] [[Aman Tuleyev]] of [[Russia]]'s [[Kemerovo Oblast]] resigns over the disaster last week at the [[Winter Cherry complex]]. Tuleyev himself lost a young relative in the fire, but had faced protests in the aftermath. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2018/apr/01/siberia-mall-fire-russian-governor-resigns-aman-tuleyev (''The Guardian'')]
**[[Association football|Football]] matches across Russia are marked with silence from fans throughout the first half to commemorate the dead. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/43612078 (BBC)]
*[[History of autonomous cars]]
**The [[United States|US]] [[National Transportation Safety Board]] criticizes [[Tesla Inc.|Tesla]] over the carmaker's release of investigative information regarding the fatal crash of a [[Tesla Model X|Model X]] in [[California]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/dr-gridlock/wp/2018/04/01/ntsb-unhappy-with-tesla-release-of-investigative-information-in-fatal-crash/ (''The Washington Post'')]
*Two buses collide head-on in [[Kuwait]], killing fifteen oil workers from [[India]], [[Egypt]], and [[Pakistan]]. Six people are injured. [https://www.thenational.ae/world/gcc/fifteen-oil-workers-killed-in-kuwait-bus-crash-1.717916 (''The National'')]
*Water shortages caused by a burst pipe in [[Thessaloniki]], [[Greece]], enter a fifth day. [http://www.ekathimerini.com/227300/article/ekathimerini/news/parts-of-thessaloniki-without-water-for-a-fifth-day-after-pipe-rupture (eKathimerini)]
*A bus crash in [[Slanic Prahova]], [[Romania]], injures 23 [[Israel]]i tourists. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/up-to-22-israeli-tourists-reportedly-injured-in-romanian-bus-accident/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
*A [[KLM]] [[Boeing 777]] flying from [[Atlanta]], [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]], to [[Amsterdam]], [[Netherlands]], encounters severe [[clear air turbulence|turbulence]] over the [[Atlantic Ocean]] causing injuries to four occupants. [http://avherald.com/h?article=4b6dcb7a&opt=0 (The Aviation Herald)]
;International relations
*[[South Korea–United States relations]]
**The governments of the [[United States]] and [[South Korea]] begin their [[Foal Eagle]] and [[Key Resolve]] military drills. [http://www.newindianexpress.com/world/2018/apr/01/south-korea-us-begin-joint-military-drills-1795537.html (''New Indian Express'')]
*[[India]]n Minister of State for External Affairs [[V. K. Singh]] travels to [[Iraq]] to reclaim the bodies of 38 workers abducted in [[Mosul]] by [[ISIL]] in 2016 after they were found in a mass grave near [[Badush]] last month. [https://www.iraqinews.com/features/indian-minister-due-in-iraq-to-reclaim-bodies-of-38-workers-killed-by-is/ (Iraqi News)]
*[[Reactions to the poisoning of Sergei and Yulia Skripal]]
** The [[Embassy of Russia, London|Embassy of Russia in London]] releases a list of 14 questions over the attack, including a question on possible [[France|French]] involvement. [https://news.sky.com/story/salisbury-poisoning-russia-issues-list-of-14-questions-for-uk-11312423 (Sky News)]
**An [[Ilyushin Il-76]] jet carrying Russian diplomats and their families who were expelled from the United States as a reaction to the poisoning arrives at [[Moscow]]'s [[Vnukovo Airport]]. [https://news.sky.com/story/salisbury-nerve-agent-attack-williamson-warns-of-new-era-of-warfare-11312398 (Sky News)]
**In an interview, [[List of ambassadors of Russia to the United Kingdom|Russian Ambassador to the United Kingdom]] [[Alexander Yakovenko (diplomat)|Alexander Yakovenko]] calls the poisoning a provocation and states that the [[Government of Russia|Russian government]] suspects British intelligence agencies of [[false flag|being behind the incident]]. [https://www.rt.com/uk/422911-uk-staged-skripal-poisoning-theory/ (RT)], [https://www.dailystar.co.uk/news/latest-news/693066/russia-spy-poisoning-britain-vladimir-putin-sergei-skripal-war-mi6-salisbury-uk-evidence (''Daily Star'')], [http://tass.com/politics/997149 (TASS)]
*[[Foreign relations of Zambia]]
**Zambian President [[Edgar Lungu]] requests that Cuba recall its ambassador, Nelson Pages Vilas, for allegedly expressing support for a new opposition party. [https://www.news24.com/Africa/News/zambia-asks-cuba-to-recall-ambassador-over-opposition-support-20180403 (News24)]
;Law and crime
*In response to the suicide of  a student, protestors attack Crossroads Higher Secondary School in [[Pampady]], [[India]], and clash with police. [http://gulfnews.com/news/asia/india/violence-in-kerala-school-after-grade-9-boy-s-suicide-1.2197898 (''Gulf News'')]
*[[Hart family crash]]
**[[California Highway Patrol]] says a crash that left five dead and three children missing after a car fell off a cliff into the sea may have been intentional. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/california-crash-killed-hart-family-believed-authorities-be-intentional-n861876 (NBC News)]
*An overnight prison riot kills seven police officers in [[Amatlán de los Reyes]], [[Veracruz]], [[Mexico]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-latin-america-43612782 (BBC)]
;Politics and elections
*[[Politics of Botswana]]
**[[Botswana]]n President [[Ian Khama]] retires from office. [[Mokgweetsi Masisi]] is inaugurated as the fifth [[President of Botswana]]. [http://www.africanews.com/2018/04/01/botswana-swears-in-its-5th-leader-president-mokgweetsi-masisi/ (Africa News)], [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-botswana-politics/botswanas-khama-steps-down-as-president-after-a-decade-at-helm-idUSKBN1H70DO (Reuters)]
*[[Costa Rican general election, 2018]], [[Recognition of same-sex unions in Costa Rica]]
**Pro-[[same-sex marriage]] candidate [[Carlos Alvarado Quesada|Carlos Alvarado]] of the [[Citizens' Action Party (Costa Rica)|Citizens' Action Party]] defeats conservative candidate [[Fabricio Alvarado Muñoz|Fabricio Alvarado]] of the [[National Restoration Party (Costa Rica)|National Restoration Party]] in the second round of voting to become the new [[President of Costa Rica]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-43617282 (BBC)]
*[[Politics of the Gambia]], [[ECOWAS military intervention in the Gambia]], [[2016–17 Gambian constitutional crisis]]
**The new government of [[the Gambia]] accuses ex-[[President of the Gambia|President]] [[Yahya Jammeh]]'s supporters of assisting and sheltering foreign militants (the [[Movement of Democratic Forces of Casamance]]). [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2018/apr/01/gambia-accuses-ex-president-yahya-jammeh-supporters-of-sheltering-rebels (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Politics of San Marino]]
**[[Matteo Ciacci]] of [[Civic 10]] and [[Stefano Palmieri]] of [[Future Republic]] take office as the [[Captains Regent of San Marino|Captains Regent]] of [[San Marino]]. [http://www.smtvsanmarino.sm/politica/2018/04/01/1-aprile-cerimonia-investitura-capitani-reggenti-palmieri-ciacci (SMTV San Marino)]
;Sports
*[[2018 Commonwealth Games]]
**The [[Commonwealth Games Federation]] places [[India at the 2018 Commonwealth Games|India]] under formal investigation for doping. [https://www.tvnz.co.nz/one-news/sport/commonwealth-games/doping-allegations-surface-commonwealth-games-india-under-investigation (TVNZ)]
*[[2018 NCAA Division I Women's Basketball Tournament]]
**[[2017–18 Notre Dame Fighting Irish women's basketball team|Notre Dame]] wins the 2018 NCAA Tournament over [[2017–18 Mississippi State Bulldogs women's basketball team|Mississippi State]] [[2018 NCAA Division I Women's Basketball Championship Game|61–58]], with the deciding points coming on a dramatic [[Three-point field goal|3-point shot]] by Arike Ogunbowale just before the final buzzer. [http://www.espn.com/womens-college-basketball/story/_/id/22992885/women-final-four-arike-ogunbowale-hits-shot-life-lead-notre-dame-fighting-irish-ncaa-title (ESPN)]
